resultText:
The task list is generated: `specs/002-prevent-booking-overlap/tasks.md`, 30 tasks, all in the required checklist format (checkbox, ID, `[P]` and story labels where they apply, file path). There is no `.specify/extensions.yml`, so no hooks ran before or after.

## Task counts

| Phase | Tasks | Count |
|---|---|---|
| Setup | T001 | 1 |
| Foundational | T002–T006 | 5 |
| US1 – create rejected on overlap (P1, MVP) | T007–T012 | 6 |
| US2 – update rejected on overlap (P2) | T013–T018 | 6 |
| US3 – simultaneous creates (P3) | T019–T021 | 3 |
| US4 – Bookings page (P4) | T022–T025 | 4 |
| Polish | T026–T030 | 5 |

## Independent test per story

- **US1**: through the gateway, create a booking, then send overlapping, touching and other-room creates, and reuse the key of a rejected create (quickstart scenarios 1–3).
- **US2**: create two non-overlapping bookings of one room, then update one to overlap, touch, and stay inside its own span (scenario 4).
- **US3**: 100 rounds of two simultaneous overlapping creates, expecting `100 201 409` (scenario 5), plus an update racing a create (scenario 6).
- **US4**: with the booking service mocked to reject with the overlap error, the form and dialog show the message and keep the input; by hand, scenario 7.

## Parallel opportunities

- Within a phase: T003/T004, T005/T006, T007–T009, T011/T012, T013–T015, T017/T018, T022–T024, T027/T028.
- Across stories: after the Foundational phase, US1, US2 and US4 share no file and can run at the same time.

## Suggested MVP

Setup, Foundational and US1 (T001–T012). After that a create can no longer double-book a room, including under a race. Moving a booking can still cause an overlap until US2 is done.

## Assumptions I made

- **New spec files instead of edits.** Four existing specs are within 25 lines of the 200-line limit, so their new cases go into sibling files (`idempotent-booking.repository.overlap.spec.ts`, `booking.repository.update.spec.ts`, `booking-create-form.overlap.spec.tsx`, `bookings-page.overlap.spec.tsx`). This differs from the plan, which lists those specs as edits.
- **US3 adds no code.** The room lock is built and unit-tested in US1 and US2, as the plan designs it. The US3 phase only proves the race against the running stack.
- **US4 specs are expected to pass on first run**, because the page already has the behaviour (research R6). A component is edited only if one of them fails.
- **Names the design left open**: `lockRoom`, `isRoomSpanTaken`, `raiseBookingOverlap` and `BookingRepository.update`.
- **Stack-dependent tasks** (T019–T021, T029, T030) need `GATEWAY_PORT` or `WEB_PORT` set in the shell. The tasks say to report "not run" rather than read a `.env` file.
- **No commit task** is listed; git is local and you decide when to commit.

The next kit step is `/speckit-analyze` for a consistency check, or `/speckit-implement` to start on the tasks.
